svg.title: Cortex Bridge Rev A4 wiring diagram
svg.desc: A Raspberry Pi 5 running Klipper connects from one of its USB-A ports to the Cortex Bridge USB-C port J1 with a USB-A to USB-C data cable. Two wires run from spare + and − terminals on the printer’s own 24 V power supply to the PWR IN screw terminal P1, + to + and − to −. The BUFFER connector CN1 connects to the 4-pin connector of the original Bambu Lab AMS filament buffer with the 4-pin buffer cable (24 V and RS-485). The buffer’s 6-pin connector goes to the first AMS unit only; up to four AMS units are daisy-chained on their 6-pin cables. Up to the coupler, filament runs in PTFE tube, 3 mm inside and 4 mm outside diameter: from each AMS outlet into an optional printed PTFE splitter (only with more than one AMS), into the buffer, into the 3 mm side of a printed PTFE tube coupler v5; from its other side, 3 mm or 2 mm ID tube runs to the toolhead extruder, where a filament cutter is required. J4 PRGRM and J7 stay empty. The Klipper computer keeps its existing USB or CAN link to the printer.
